hints: Find the tiny slice labelled cell division and follow the circular arrow to see what comes just after it. The biggest slice after division is for growth, not for copying DNA.
Remember the order of interphase after division: G1 for growth, then S for DNA synthesis, then G2 for preparation, then mitosis.
walkthrough:
**Spot mitosis and work out the direction**

Look at the pie chart. The very tiny slice is cell division, which is cytokinesis. The slice just before it labelled D is mitosis (nuclear division). The circular arrow runs clockwise, so the cycle goes: C to D to cell division to A to B and back to C.

**Recall what interphase does**

Most of the cycle is interphase, made of three phases in order:
$$G1 \rightarrow S \rightarrow G2$$
G1 is cell growth and making new organelles and proteins. S is DNA replication to make sister chromatids. G2 is growth and preparation for mitosis.

**Match size to phase and pick S**

After cell division comes A, the largest slice. That is G1, the longest growth phase. Next comes B, where DNA is replicated. That is S phase. Next comes C, the preparation time before mitosis. That is G2. So DNA replication is phase B.

options.A: A is the largest slice just after cell division, so it is G1 for cell growth, not DNA replication.
options.B: B is the S phase of interphase, between G1 and G2, when semi-conservative DNA replication occurs.
options.C: C comes just before mitosis, so it is G2 for final growth and preparation, DNA has already been copied.
options.D: D comes just before cytokinesis, so it is mitosis when chromosomes separate, not when DNA is replicated.
